name: Philip W. Anderson
summary: American theoretical physicist known for work on localization, superexchange, and cuprate superconductivity.

name: John van Vleck
summary: American theoretical physicist and Anderson's graduate supervisor at Harvard.

name: Harvard University
summary: Ivy League university in Cambridge, Massachusetts where Anderson studied.

name: Bell Labs
summary: Industrial research laboratory where Anderson worked for 35 years.

name: Princeton University
summary: University where Anderson became a full-time professor after leaving Bell Labs.

name: Nobel Prize in Physics 1977
summary: 1977 Nobel Prize awarded to Anderson, Van Vleck, and Mott for magnetic and electronic systems.

name: Cuprate Superconductors
summary: Class of high-temperature superconducting materials discovered in 1986.

name: G. Baskaran
summary: Physicist who collaborated with Anderson on RVB theory of superconductivity.

name: Maurice Rice
summary: Physicist at ETH Zurich and long-time collaborator of Anderson.

name: Phuan Ong
summary: Experimentalist at Princeton who collaborated with Anderson on vortex liquid studies.

name: Ted Geballe
summary: Physicist and Bell Labs alumnus who informed Anderson about cuprate discovery.

name: Georg Bednorz
summary: Co-discoverer of cuprate superconductivity with Alex Muller.

name: Alex Muller
summary: Co-discoverer of cuprate superconductivity with Georg Bednorz.

name: Aspen Center for Physics
summary: Physics center where Anderson spent time rethinking cuprate theory.
